plain_description.what: Exploratory sweep with no judge calls. The tree is built from embeddings alone, with no declared subject labels. The test counted how many of its split points pass the statistical significance check (the 'certificate'). It then tried six construction changes one at a time (wider embeddings, pruning, removing top principal components, a different split bar, and combinations).
plain_description.why: It asks whether the tree's structure is real and certifiable, or whether only a small part of it passes the significance check.
plain_description.information: If some change raised the certified count fairly, it would give a better recipe for building trees. If not, the record count is the honest ceiling. Result: done, exploratory. No change beat the record's 16 of 69 certified splits under a common null. Gains only appeared when a change also weakened the null. A later re-draw corrected the reading: the certified 'fringe' changes from draw to draw (10 to 16 sites), and only 5 core splits are certified on every draw. Nothing was promoted.
